name: Flower and Scorpion
description: Flower & Scorpion is an exotic variation of the domino game Bergen, traditionally associated with North African and Middle Eastern social circles. It combines standard domino-matching mechanics with the unpredictable element of dice rolling. Before each round, two pairs of dice are rolled to determine the 'Flower' (a lucky number that grants bonuses) and the 'Scorpion' (a cursed number that imposes penalties). Players act as members of a caravan, trying to match ends of the line (The Caravan) while navigating the hazards of the Scorpion's sting.

content.text: Flower & Scorpion is an exotic variation of the domino game Bergen, traditionally associated with North African and Middle Eastern social circles. It combines standard domino-matching mechanics with the unpredictable element of dice rolling. Before each round, two pairs of dice are rolled to determine the 'Flower' (a lucky number that grants bonuses) and the 'Scorpion' (a cursed number that imposes penalties). Players act as members of a caravan, trying to match ends of the line (The Caravan) while navigating the hazards of the Scorpion's sting.

The game is believed to have developed in Morocco and the surrounding Maghreb region during the colonial era. It likely blended French/German domino games (Bergen) with local gambling traditions involving Backgammon dice found in local bars and cafes.
2 to 4 players. Best with 4 (playing as individuals).
One pair of 'Flower' dice (e.g., Green) and one pair of 'Scorpion' dice (e.g., Red).
Each player receives 5 or 6 tiles (depending on player count). Remaining tiles are placed face-down in the 'Oasis'.
